extracted.intended_audience: general readers, film scholars, and researchers interested in film censorship and banned films
extracted.subtask_short: list of banned films by reason
extracted.subtask_description: A country-by-country catalogue of films that have been banned, with the official or reported reasons given for each ban (e.g., sexual content, political criticism, blasphemy, extreme violence). Useful for comparative study of censorship grounds and patterns across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic/extreme violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for graphic, extremely violent or high-impact violent content (phrases used: "extremely violent content", "gore, violence", "high impact scary violence").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples throughout the list include Cannibal Holocaust (extremely violent content), The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (high impact scary violence), Ichi The Killer (high impact violence and cruelty), The Green Elephant (graphic violence). Several bans were later lifted or modified with cuts or age restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual violence involving young people / minors
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for sexual violence involving young people (explicit mention: "sexual violence involving young people", "sexual assault on a minor").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Megan Is Missing (sexual violence involving young people), Kite (graphic sexual assault on a minor). Often cited as a specific ground for prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexualized violence fused with sexual gratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because a scene "fuses an act of extreme violence with sexual gratification" (sexual violence combined with sexual arousal/gratification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostel: Part II was banned on this ground until the offending scene was excised; rationale is that sexualized violence is particularly objectionable to classification boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting/supporting use of violence to compel sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it "tends to promote and support the use of violence to compel any person to submit to sexual conduct."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precise phrasing appears for I Spit on Your Grave (2010) and similar titles; classification authorities viewed the film as endorsing or normalizing coercive sexual violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necrophilia / sexual conduct with a dead person
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because "the publication promotes and supports sexual conduct with or upon the body of a dead person" or for trying to "normalise necrophilia."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited for Nekromantik 2 (New Zealand) where both the film and additional material were judged to normalize necrophilia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bestiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film "promotes and supports bestiality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vase de Noces was explicitly banned on this ground; classification authorities single out bestiality as a prohibitive category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploitation of nudity and flippant treatment of real tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for "exploit[ing] the nudity of women and present[ing] real and tragic events in a flippant and offensive way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Love Camp 7 (unedited DVD) was banned for combining exploitation of nudity with insensitivity to real tragic events; authorities consider context and tone as part of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pornography / obscene sexual content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for being pornography or pornographic in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I Am Curious (Yellow) was noted as banned because of pornography; some jurisdictions differentiate explicit pornographic works from mainstream films and may ban accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blasphemy / religiously sensitive themes / depiction of prophets
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for blasphemous content or religiously sensitive material (e.g., depiction of prophets or content offensive to religious believers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Da Vinci Code and Noah were banned in some countries for religiously sensitive themes; islands/states with strong religious sensibilities often cite these grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offending religious institutions or beliefs / disrespect to religion or royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film was deemed "critical of the Catholic Church", "disrespectful towards the King", or otherwise offensive to dominant religious or cultural institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The King and I (could be construed as disrespectful towards the King of Thailand), films critical of the Catholic Church banned in Samoa; ban rationale can be institutional (church/state) sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBT content / depiction of gay, lesbian, or transgender characters/relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for depicting gay/lesbian/transgender relationships or characters (mentions include "brief lesbian kiss", characters with same-sex partners, and display of a transgender flag).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lightyear, Eternals, Onward, and Barbie are cited in various jurisdictions as banned or cut due to LGBT content; OIC/Arab League and some other countries specifically target LGBT representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting ideas not in line with local cultures/values / undermining public morals
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for "promoting ideas and beliefs that are not in line with the cultures and values" or for "undermining public morals" / "not corresponding to traditional values."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barbie and other titles were banned under these general cultural-morality rationales; wording is broad and applied to varied content (sexuality, gender, politics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of an Israeli actor / nationality of performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because an actor was Israeli (e.g., "Banned ... because actress Haya Harareet was Israeli").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ben-Hur is repeatedly noted as banned across Arab League states for this reason; national/ethnic origin of cast has been grounds for bans in some political contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political criticism / subversiveness / anti-government content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for political reasons: critical depiction of the regime, portraying coups, encouraging communism, criticism of government or military, or being "subversive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous examples under Communist or military regimes (e.g., Poland, Spain under Franco, Paraguay under Stroessner, Pakistan), where film content challenging authority or portraying dissent was prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racist/xenophobic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for being racist or xenophobic (explicit mention: "banned due to accusations of being xenophobic and racist").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District 9 was banned in Nigeria for alleged xenophobia and racism; some bans arise from concerns the film insults or misrepresents particular groups or nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real animal cruelty / actual on-screen animal killings
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because of actual on-screen killings of animals or demonstrated animal cruelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannibal Holocaust was banned in some jurisdictions for containing real animal killings; on-screen animal harm is treated as a distinct and severe ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion/normalization of torture and sadistic violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned on grounds that the work "tend[s] to promote and support acts of torture and the infliction of extreme violence and extreme cruelty" or for "torture and sadistic violence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostel: Part II and similar titles faced bans under statutory language referencing torture and sadism (e.g., s3(2)(f) of New Zealand's Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation likely to erode empathy / invites enjoyment of cruelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it "tacit[ly] invit[es] to enjoy cruel and violent behavior" and is "likely to lead to an erosion of empathy for some viewers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maniac was prohibited on this reasoning; classification bodies may assess not just content but likely psychological/social effects on viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrary to public decency or public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because content would be "contrary to public decency and undesirable to public interest."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tarzoon: Shame of the Jungle and similar titles were banned under this broad decency/public interest rationale; often used when a film offends prevailing moral norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content likely to cause severe physical reactions in audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because screenings caused extreme physical reactions in viewers (e.g., vomiting, fainting), cited as evidence of harmful impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ichi The Killer was banned in Norway after reported incidents at a festival where viewers vomited and fainted; some authorities consider extreme visceral reactions in classification decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit sexual acts / detailed close-ups of sexual activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned or required cuts because of explicit close-ups or graphic depiction of sexual acts (e.g., "fingering, ejaculation, fellatio").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taiwan's Love was released only after cuts removing close-ups of intercourse and oral sex; classification often targets graphic sexual imagery even if between consenting adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting drug use among impressionable youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it "might encourage the impressionable youth ... to take up" drug use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up in Smoke was banned in South Africa on the ground it might encourage marijuana use among youth; encourages authorities to consider influence on young audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation, libel, or portrayals leading to legal action
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned or seized because the film contained material judged defamatory or insulting to named individuals or institutions (legal/ libel grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rocío was seized and banned in Spain over accusations of libel and insult to a mayor and religious sensibilities; courts may intervene on defamation grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite 'objectionable content' including pedophilia, extreme sexual violence, necrophilia
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned as containing "objectionable content" listed as offensive depictions of sexual violence, pedophilia, extreme violence, necrophilia and/or other content that is offensive and abhorrent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Serbian Film was banned on such composite grounds; classification statements sometimes list multiple severe sexual/criminal acts to justify prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tampering with historical facts / alleged historical inaccuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned or restricted for allegedly "tampering with historical facts" or presenting contested historical narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bell Bottom (reported) was banned for alleged tampering with historical facts; some bans arise from perceived harm to national historical memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual content judged inappropriate to local culture or religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because sexual content was judged "inappropriate and contradictory to Christian beliefs and Samoan culture" or similar cultural/religious statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milk was initially banned in Samoa for being inappropriate to Christian beliefs; cultural fit is a recurring criterion in many countries with conservative social norms.
